input.case_summary: Hospitalization and surgical claim of Rs 1,45,000 for bilateral cataract surgery rejected under Clause 4.2 pre-existing condition exclusion, despite uninterrupted 36-month policy tenure and treating surgeon medical certificate confirming acute onset.

citations: IRDAI Master Circular on Health Insurance (2024)
output.reasoning: Policy has exceeded the 36-month moratorium period under IRDAI 2024 guidelines. Pre-existing exclusion cannot be invoked post 3 years of continuous renewal. Claim rejection violates Section 45.

input.case_summary: Double deduction of Rs 5,000 occurred during UPI QR payment at merchant terminal. The merchant settlement record confirms receipt of only single credit. Bank has failed to auto-reversal within the mandatory RBI T+1 timeline and refused penalty compensation.

citations: RBI Circular DPSS.CO.PD No.629/02.01.014/2019-20 (Harmonisation of TAT and customer compensation)
output.reasoning: RBI turn-around time mandate requires auto-reversal by T+1. Overdue by 12 days; customer is entitled to Rs 100/day compensation beyond turnaround time.

input.case_summary: Flight 6E-241 (BOM to DEL) cancelled 2 hours prior to scheduled departure. Carrier refused alternate flight on partner carriers, declined hotel accommodation, and issued an expiring travel credit note instead of statutory full cash refund.

citations: DGCA Civil Aviation Requirement (CAR) Section 3, Series M, Part IV
output.reasoning: DGCA CAR Section 3 stipulates full refund within 7 days plus passenger compensation of Rs 10,000 for cancellation without 24h prior notification.

input.case_summary: Postpaid fiber and SIM service cancelled with written confirmation on April 4, 2026. Airtel continued recurring monthly generation of Rs 1,178 plus late payment interest for two successive billing cycles.

citations: Telecom Disputes Settlement and Appellate Tribunal (TDSAT) Rulings
output.reasoning: TRAI regulations prohibit service provider billing past verified termination request confirmation date. Negative credit reporting threats are unlawful.

input.case_summary: Builder failed to offer physical handover of 3BHK unit by scheduled completion date of December 2024. Promoter refuses to disburse monthly delay interest at SBI MCLR+2% under Section 18 of Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act 2016.

citations: Supreme Court of India: Newtech Promoters vs State of UP (2021)
output.reasoning: Section 18 gives allottee absolute unconditional right to monthly interest until possession. Force majeure clauses cannot be extended arbitrarily.

input.case_summary: High-end headphones ordered under Prime delivery verified as counterfeit by authorized Sony Service Center. Amazon seller declined replacement or refund alleging item tampered by buyer.

citations: Consumer Protection Act 2019 Section 2(9) and Section 2(47)
output.reasoning: Marketplace platform shares joint liability for counterfeit goods sold through fulfilled channels under E-Commerce Rules 2020.

input.case_summary: Re-issue application File No. DL108492819 stuck at Police Verification stage for over 90 days despite spotless verification history, violating citizen charter SLA.

citations: Public Records Citizen Charter SLA Guidelines
output.reasoning: Citizen Charter sets maximum SLA of 21 days for standard police verification. 90-day delay constitutes administrative deficiency.

input.case_summary: Hospital charged Rs 48,000 in unitemized surgical consumables and billed room tariff at both admission and discharge days contrary to Clinical Establishments Act and CGHS rates.

citations: National Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission (NCDRC) Overbilling Precedents
output.reasoning: NCDRC guidelines prohibit charging room tariff twice for calendar day of admission and discharge when total duration is under 24 hours for that bracket.
